feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 0 (4 cm span, 12 mm sensors, y=0.05, mass 0.8) lost the line 1.0 to 2.0 times per run. Iteration 1 (±3 cm span, 16 mm sensors, y=0.04, mass 0.7) lost it about 1.0 per run on all tracks. Iteration 2 (same, y=0.03) also stayed at 1.0 per run, with steering oscillation between 0.07 and 0.13. So the span and forward offset are not the limit. I held the controller fixed (kp 2.5, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5) so this change is isolated. Decision rules for the next race: (1) If line_loss_events fall to 0.5 or less on the s-bend and slalom and max_error stays under 0.06 m, keep mass at 0.6 kg and check whether completion_time is approaching 3 s. (2) If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with the lighter robot, the response is overshooting; return to mass 0.7 kg and try y=0.035 m. (3) If line_loss_events stay near 1.0 per run at 0.6 kg, the next test is a wheel change, not a sensing change. Check wheel slip on starts before raising wheel_track further.
requested_changes: Keep mass at 0.6 kg with wheel_track 0.14 m and sensors at y=0.03 m with the ±3 cm span. Basis: iteration 2 kept line loss at 1.0 per run at 0.7 kg, and mass is the untested dynamics lever.

If line loss persists at 0.6 kg, change wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m with mass 0.6 kg. Basis: iterations 0 to 2 showed sensor span and offset do not remove the single bend loss, so turn authority is the next lever.

If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.2 at 0.6 kg, return to mass 0.7 kg and move sensor y to 0.035 m. Basis: iteration 2 oscillation was 0.07 to 0.13 at y=0.03, so there is room before jitter becomes a problem.
